newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper ends firmer, sees new contract highs.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper ends firmer, sees new contract highs.

text.p: COMEX copper futures ended firmer Wednesday, setting new life-of-contract highs in the June, September, October and December contracts before gains were pared on profit-taking, traders said.

Brisk July to September trading was noted due to switches, and this spread was set to come in because there was still a large amount of open interest in the July that needed to be rolled forward, dealers said.
June COMEX slipped into a brief backwardation to July, but the two months ended in contango.

Much of the strength in copper futures on both sides of the Atlantic was coming from the LME cash to three months backwardation which widened Wednesday by $10 to $101/$105, John Tyree of FIMAT Futures said.
"LME (three months) will make it over $2,600 a tonne and stay there. There is enough tightness out there and I think the summer slowdown will not be enough to kill it," Tyree said.
LME three months briefly popped above $2,600 but slipped back later.

July COMEX settled 0.75 cent firmer at 121.95 cents per lb, traded 123.10 to 120.35 cents. Spot June went out 0.45 cent higher at 121.55 cents, off the high of 122.50 cents, the best showing for a spot contract since early May last year.
September, due to become the most active contract, settled at 119.65 cents, up 0.25 cent on the day.

In a special copper report by LME ring dealer Rudolf Wolff, analyst Martin Squires said copper had the potential to rally to $2,715 a tonne in the third quarter before falling back below $2,000 in the longer term as new production comes on stream and exchange stocks rise.
LME stocks rose 300 tonnes to 122,525 tonnes Wednesday, a nominal hike but the first increase for a while.
